newsitem.title: USA: Conn.'s Blumenthal to seek re-election as atty gen.
newsitem.headline: Conn.'s Blumenthal to seek re-election as atty gen.

text.p: Connecticut Attorney General Richard Blumenthal said Tuesday he will seek re-election for a third term next year.
A Democrat, Blumenthal had been regarded as a leading candidate to unseat Republican Gov. John Rowland, but had been non-committal about next year's gubernatorial race.
Blumenthal, 51, has been attorney general since 1991.
"I have decided to seek re-election as attorney general of the state of Connecticut in 1998," Blumenthal said in a statement.
He said it was "enormously satisfying" to serve as attorney general.
Since taking office, Blumenthal has been a vigorous foe of the tobacco industry and advocate of rapid deregulation of the state's electric utilities industry.

Other Connecticut Democrats who have been thinking about running for governor include Bridgeport Mayor Joseph Ganim, House Speaker Tom Ritter, U.S. Rep. Barbara Kennelly, and former state comptroller Bill Curry.
Curry was the Democrats' unsuccessful nominee in 1994.
